Various infrastructure projects intended to enhance water supply are either delayed or in early planning stages. Desalination plants are in development, but they will only partially address the water shortage.

In this deceptive scheme, fraudsters make small deposits to build trust before compelling victims to approve larger payments. The bank recommends customers to be vigilant against suspicious communications, immediately block any questionable contacts, and report any unexpected transactions to prevent falling victim to this manipulation.

Syria reopens 1,600-year-old Byzantine church complex after restoration
description: After extensive restoration, the Deir Samaan Citadel, a remarkable ancient religious complex in northern Syria, has reopened its doors to visitors. Established in the fifth century, this site holds immense significance for Christian pilgrims. Having endured damage from natural calamities, conflict, and neglect, recent efforts aimed to repair visitor pathways and rehabilitate essential facilities. This reopening forms part of a larger initiative to encourage tourism in the Aleppo province.

He argues that this decision diminishes the prestige of the domestic tournament, as domestic players' performances might lose value with top players being diverted to the India A team. Vengsarkar advocates for an earlier acclimatisation trip for the main team instead.

title: Buried under Greenland’s ice: The secret US Army base Nasa rediscovered in 2024
description: The hidden U.S. military base, Camp Century, built beneath Greenland's glaciers during the late 1950s, has resurfaced in a NASA radar scan revealing its intricate layout. Known for housing a nuclear reactor and various toxic materials, the site poses significant environmental risks as Greenland's ice diminishes. This finding compels us to confront the implications of historical military operations in light of our planet's shifting climate.

title: CJP raises ‘phone hacking’ doubts, to continue protest
description: Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das from Cockroach Janata Party addressed journalists regarding their recent detention. They expressed fears about potential phone hacking after being separated from their devices by police. The activists emphasized their commitment to protesting until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns and accountability is established. Allegations of police misconduct, including the assault of protesters and detaining of student leaders, were also raised.

title: Couple rejects $131,000 offer for data center power line on their property
description: Jerry Zelenka has turned down an offer from American Transmission Company for a power line on his property. The proposal involves clearing trees and demolishing several buildings near his home, prompting Zelenka's concerns. He feels the compensation does not reflect the value of his property or the destruction planned. Zelenka fears the use of eminent domain if an agreement is not reached.

title: Florida family protects 498-acre cattle ranch in $7.48m conservation deal
description: A 498-acre cattle ranch known as Turnpike Dairy has been protected from future development through a conservation easement. The agreement allows the managing family to continue agricultural operations on the property. Martin County contributed $3.74 million towards the $7.48 million deal to preserve the land. This conservation effort is part of Florida’s Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, which protects working farms.

title: Oregon blimp hangar sold for $1 after storm damage; air museum set to reopen
description: An 83-year-old World War II-era blimp hangar in Oregon, US, was sold for just $1 after a storm tore a 200-foot hole in its roof in December 2025. The historic building, which houses the Tillamook Air Museum, was purchased by a nonprofit organisation and is set to reopen on October 29 after nearly 10 months of closure.

title: Who gets to be a genius? Matilda effect and the women missing from science
Colorado woman protects 18,484 acres of family ranch once listed for $100 million
description: A Colorado woman has permanently protected 18,484 acres of her family's cattle ranch, once listed for $100 million, from future development. Susan Nottingham's decision preserves land her parents spent over 60 years assembling, along with historic water rights linked to the Colorado River. The agreement also protects wildlife habitats while allowing the ranch to continue agricultural operations.

title: Washington farmer challenges $618,000 irrigation penalties in state Supreme Court
description: Ron Fodé, a dedicated farmer from Washington State, is fighting against hefty penalties threatening his agricultural livelihood due to irrigation practices. The conflict arose in 2017 over water rights for his crops, leading to the Department of Ecology rejecting his irrigation assistance applications. This has resulted in penalties totaling $618,000.

title: Taylor Swift’s $4m Nashville education centre now showcases local student art
description: In 2012, Taylor Swift donated $4 million to create an education center at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. This center focuses on engaging children and families with the history of country music. Currently, it hosts an exhibition called Connection featuring works by students and artists from Friends Life Community. Participants learn letterpress printing techniques and create their own unique posters.
